Regional differences in the United Kingdom

The United Kingdom comprises four distinct countries. How does UK fiscal policy affect these countries differently?

Text
​

Regional differences in the United Kingdom

The United Kingdom (UK) consists of four countries—England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. Despite their geographical proximity and very strong economic integration, differences exist.

The table below illustrates some economic data about the UK.

CountryTotal population (million)Disposable income per capitaGovernment spending per capitaGovernment revenue per capita
England57.1£\sterling£23 338£\sterling£11 549£\sterling£14 051
Scotland3.1£\sterling£20 854£\sterling£13 881£\sterling£13 140
Wales5.4£\sterling£18 652£\sterling£13 401£\sterling£10 473
Northern Ireland1.9£\sterling£18 685£\sterling£14 062£\sterling£10 257
UK totals67.6£22 789£11 897£13 703

  1. Define the term disposable income per capita. [2]

  2. Calculate the total government spending in Wales. [2]

  3. Using data from the table, explain why public spending in the UK in 2022 can be considered a redistribution policy. [3]


The table illustrates some of the major sources of public sector spending for the UK in 2022.

SourceAmount in billion £\sterling£
Health and social care167.9
State pensions110.6
Debt interest83.0
Education77.0
Universal credit71.3
Investment56.4
Defense32.4
  1. State two examples of investment spending that a government can undertake. [2]


In 2022, public sector total revenues were £\sterling£987.5 billion, while its spending totalled £\sterling£1 087 billion.

  1. Calculate the budget deficit for 2022. [2]

  2. Explain why a persistent budget deficit might lead to increased spending on debt interest. [3]


At the end of 2022, the UK national debt was 100.4% of its GDP.

Some politicians argued that the UK government should aim for a substantial budget surplus for most of this decade to significantly reduce the burden of debt interest payments on the annual budget. They contended that, by freeing up crucial resources, lower levels of national debt would promote long-term economic growth.

    1. Suggest one reason supporting the argument that the UK government should reduce the country’s national debt. [2]

    2. Suggest one reason opposing the argument that the UK government should reduce the country’s national debt. [2]

    3. To what extent is the argument that the UK government should reduce the country’s national debt true? [4]
